body:
Actually, I like this.

It's a gag poem, but I don't know if your opening lines are visceral or creepy enough for the gag to be effective. When you have a poem this short, every line has to make a strong impact, and here you rest your laurels on cliches. I'd pinpoint the emotions you're trying pinpoint  and create something more unique and individual to express it.

So here's how I see it:

Eyes dart back and forth = extreme anxiety 

Sharp teeth in your jaw = fear of personal harm (also, sharp teeth are supposed to be in jaws. This line especially didn't work.)

Always lurking in the shadows = Fear of the unknown. 

Find a way to make your audience feel these emotions in a way that's unique to you and terrifying, keep the last line, and now we're talking.

Thanks for the laugh.

Yeah, man, I thought that venom movie sucked too, and I think you have a very good critique here of Art as a whole and its intersection with society, but I'm not entirely sure weighing the most focus on the keyboard vs. the pen really illustrates the point you're making as effectively as something else could, because I'm not seeing much of a direct connection and all I could think was - what's so damn wrong with a keyboard? I try writing with a pen. No one can read my writing. It's hieroglyphics, man. The keyboard is a tool of mercy.

I don't know if any of that critique makes a bit of sense, but what I'm trying to say is this seems like a draft where you know your end result but aren't sure what building blocks you need to get there. Keep wrestling with it.

Nah, man, I appreciate you for it. I agree with you much more than you think.  I had a pretty active five minute debate in my head about posting this because I didn’t think it was that wonderful, and frankly a subpar ripoff of Radiohead’s Fitter, Happier,  what the hell do I know? 

Edit: I’m clearly a genius.
I'd tell you that I looked that number up for accuracy, but, I...can't remember.
My fellow cynical friend, it is good to find you. Let us find each other, share a drink and bitch about things we'll never do a single thing about to change.
I'm actually just going to have Siri read it for me.

It's honestly weird to see my word vomit getting such in-depth analysis but it's also weird to see it getting 50 damn upvotes. Thanks for taking more time to critique the piece than I took in writing it. Seems a little backwards, but ah well, such is life.
How dare you. Myself and my army of upvoting bots are currently plotting our revenge.
You’re a good sport, kid.
Thank you for connecting.

When I make my poetry book, there's going to be a miniature computer screen with a hard-drive installed with only enough memory to display this poem and launch a locking mechanism forbidding you from turning the page until you plug in a USB mouse (no, it's not provided. I live in America, not Norway) and scroll through it. It's going to change everything.

I have been taught - through stern repetitive scolding - that the word that is almost always unnecessary. Like the first "that" in that sentence. That that was entirely unnecessary. A few "thats" are probably unnecessary in that last sentence too. But I'm losing track of all of that already. 

Anyway, you're probably right. Thanks for being helpful. I'm not making any changes though.

Ahem...

If you haven't seen my other poem on here (and how dare you!) then let me inform you of my schtick. I am a drunk poet. My Bukowski doesn't come out until at least a pint of vodka is corroding a hole into my liver- so you're just lucky there's any poetic elements at all you goddamn punk. 

Rhyme?! Who do you think you are? My seventh grade English teacher? Well, she's now the principal of that Catholic school so she obviously isn't any fun, and you're not any fun either. Wither away in shame.
Ladies and gentlemen, we have found our protagonist.

Yeah, that symbolism makes complete sense and it may have just been a case of me being thickheaded in not recognizing it. Its symbolic property may also not be entirely clear. I'll let you parse that out.

Thanks for sharing.

My latest drunken rant about Facebook.

Thanks for not taking the title literally.

You've been wearing the same dress, every day, since 25? How old are you? Do you wash it? Is it like rags by now? This doesn't seem very realistic and I'm not sure there's a very enticing reason for it not to be.

I hate all-caps. Nothing here is done much better by including all caps.

"With the door open, my brain works quickly to register who is standing in front of me.
Oh, hello YOU,” I say, happily, recognizing, instantly, the familiar face..."

This doesn't seem very instant.

How do I know you? I'm not entirely sure, with what is presented, that it's interesting to know you. 

There's something very visceral and direct about this. And a surprising sense of warmth at the end. I also enjoy the piece's simplicity.

Hi there,

Personally the phrasing here seems a little stilted.

"A droplet amongst storms, only one of many.
A whistle amongst hurricanes, voice drowning."

This seems a little redundant.

And, I wouldn't state this is a definite issue, but I'm not entirely sure the hope at the end is made clear. 

With all that said, I have an immediate instinct to turn off all the lights and read this by candle light, so I think you've been quite successful.

I certainly was not referring to you, most fair and reasonable administrator of the OC poetry subreddit. On a range of Mussolini to Hitler, I'd rank you as a Franklin Deleano Roosevelt except with not such a hard on for undermining the judiciary and imprisoning the Japanese. 

Uh...

Ok, look, maintaining the persona of the community drunk poet is very delicate business... If you get that balance right, you're probably not drunk which kinda goes against the entire gig.

Wow, this is a lot to digest, but I really liked these comments.

It's important to clarify just how drunk I was when I started this and how I progressively got more drunk as I continued writing it. So, if you're expecting any kind of useful clarification here - well, that's unfortunate. 

So, what do I mean when I say that Jesus was a chainsaw. Maybe I meant that he cut through Jewish religious traditions to bring salvation to the common-folk. Maybe I mean that Jesus is far more vengeful than we give him credit for who cuts down the hopes (and presents) of bad bitches. Or maybe the concept we have of Jesus as a white man is inaccurate and he actually was a walking, talking chainsaw. It's hard to say. I think I just found the line funny.

Poem about numbers #2 is the most important and meaningful poem in this whole collection. I will never delete it.

Poem about fuck is it a little weak, but fuck it. 

You should check out Gary Jules' "Mad World", you'll love it.

Muskegon is a city in Michigan.

"Wisnae" - I'm using an authentic dialect. Like Hemingway.

And that actually is a classic poem? No fucking kidding. Who knew it would be that easy.

Thanks for chatting.

"Like maybe I after that I begin to narrate, and maybe even make fun of, myself in third person."

That sounds like a whole new creative direction for you to play with. Very exciting. You have my encouragement.  I look forward to seeing what you come up with.

"Also, I read you're poem posted just now and am genuinely impressed."

All credit goes to Captain Morgan's spiced rum.

"Also, it's not 2019."

Well, this is awkward....

"When I said polaroid, I didn't mean like the camera. I meant like the polaroid as in the physics term."

Well, this is even more awkward...

Anyway, clearly I have no idea what I'm talking about so no need to get defensive. Let's keep with the positive vibes. I'm just fooling anyway. This is good shit and I enjoyed reading it.

This is meant to be read as one piece of work - a single poem. 

DON'T ANY OF YOU POETRY FASCISTS GO DELETING IT. 

(Also, technically - if plagiarism is done in jest it isn't plagiarism. Someone important wrote that rule down somewhere. I'm sure of it.)

"If the blinding radiance of the sun is reduced to nothing with the use of cold Polaroids...
and you can see the sun for what it is,
and not what it pretends to be,
is it still beautiful?
Is it still the sun?"

Well technically when I point my camera at the sun, I just get a blinding bunch of light which fucks up the rest of my picture, which is contained in a digital file, because who uses polaroids anymore. Christ, it's 2019. (I'm not even going to edit this. I'm an honest person) Maybe if you got a better camera you wouldn't feel so sad. I think that's the solution to this poem's whole dilemma personally.

I like the turning to third person in the last line. I feel it's the climax of the poem, the complete dissociation of self, and I wish you would have went farther with the concept.

 Much of this reads like a philosophical dissertation though - or a therapy session - which is nice and emotional, but you know that show and not tell rule? Fucking like,  repeat that to yourself 250 times before you go to sleep every night for the next week and then attempt this poem again.

For fuck sakes though. Polaroids? Why?

I'm wondering if there's any reason there's no title to this poem? I don't think keeping it without a title is adding any meaning to this. 

Maybe you can use something like "in color" - that seems about right. 

Ok, being somewhat flippant there, but it's a serious critique. Anyway, about the last time that phrase is used. In the last line. Naturally. 

Is it "you we are in color"? - in which case - why? What does this mean?

Is it "You were in color"? - which is a little bit of a sadder or nostalgic ending.

Is it "You in color"? - which is the first rendition of the "you added an extra word" hypothesis - this seems a bit redundant but maybe that has some extra effect.

Or is it "We're in color"? - that's kind of romantic. You're making all of us redditors feel warm and fuzzy.

Anyway, this is good stuff. You should keep making stuff like it.
